registry_info.name: field_room
registry_info.description: Wave-2 synthesis (doc/plans/ARTIFACT_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md, 'field room'). A SERIES built out of force_field_visualizer, vector_field_grid, vector_fields, weather_vector_field, force_field_zone and particle_flow_swarm: ONE vector function stood up and read four ways at once - glyph arrows, streamlines, a population riding it, and the bare law on a plate.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel synthesis builders never share one JSON. This artifact does not replace any of its six sources and must not be substituted for them: the walk-scale encounter with one field artifact you can actually reach into is the curriculum's spine, and nothing here can be touched. The row is for a room that wants the comparison.

field_room.name: Field Room
field_room.description: One vector field, four readings, side by side on a 2.4 m wall. Top left: an 8x8 lattice of glyph arrows, one local sample per cell. Top right: sixteen streamlines integrated through the same field, both ways from their seeds. Bottom left: 120 bodies dropped on the field and advected, each with a short upstream wake, so density says what the curves cannot. Bottom right: the equation, etched, with the field's value at one probe point printed as two numbers. F is computed by a single function and the four panels differ only in what they do with it. `law` turns which rule the space obeys and all four readings turn together; `coding` turns what the tint claims, held fixed across three different kinds of picture. Use #law: and #coding:.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: footprint_cells is a COUNT, not a [w,d] pair - a pair crashes the placement engine. The measured mesh extent is 2.42 m wide x 2.55 m tall x 0.34 m deep, identical at every value of both axes because the backing board, the two feet and the four panel plates are unconditional; only the 0.34 m depth of the feet and the 2.42 m of board touch the floor, so 3 x 1 cells are actually occupied. Front clearance 3 is the reading distance: the wall is 2.55 m tall and the four panels are meant to be taken in together, which cannot be done from 1 m away. wall_backing true because nothing on the back face is drawn.

field_room.qfep_connection: F as a rule over a domain, and then the harder half: a rule can only be met as a picture, and the picture is a choice. Four readings of one function stand side by side and each is blind to something the others show - the glyphs cannot say where a body ends up, the population cannot say anything about the field where no body went, the streamlines cannot show density, and the plate shows all of it and draws none of it. The dark spot is not an accident of any one drawing; it moves when the drawing changes, which is the only way to see that it is there at all.
field_room.relationships: Synthesised from [[force_field_visualizer]], [[vector_field_grid]], [[vector_fields]], [[weather_vector_field]], [[force_field_zone]] and [[particle_flow_swarm]] - the corpus's largest un-synthesised family, six artifacts that drew the same object six ways across four registry files and three sequences, and were never once in the same room. WHAT THEY LEARNED, and what this exhibits. [[force_field_visualizer]] coined `law` and found its four values are four different SPATIAL GRAMMARS rather than four settings - gravity the only one where position carries no information at all - and, building its longhand plates, that an inverse-square field spans four decades so a LINEAR ramp prints one white dot on a black square. That finding is load-bearing here: it is why both the tint and the arrow LENGTH are log-normalised, since the source's own linear clamp saturates almost every arrow on this lattice. [[vector_field_grid]] coined `coding` for this family - what the tint CLAIMS as against what it shows - and found that mark length must keep carrying magnitude at every value, so `uniform` withholds the colour without withholding the magnitude. It also measured the dilution that governs this whole family: arrows on an otherwise empty plane are a thin subject, crop before believing INERT. [[vector_fields]] took `coding` character for character and found that a shared word is only honest when siblings measure alike - and that the SAME value can be right in one body and wrong in another for a reason about the MESH, since its cone has an apex where its sibling's box has none. [[weather_vector_field]] refused both `field` and `law` because its field never changes - it is always A + B - and found that every instrument in a room is a different read of one vector, which is this room's thesis with the instruments swapped for drawings. [[force_field_zone]] took `law` and REFUSED three of its four values, because a uniform volume cannot be a point charge, a dipole or a vortex; its own list is refused here for the mirror reason (see dna.declined). [[particle_flow_swarm]] is DECLARED a pair with [[vector_field_grid]] - one draws the field, the other rides it - and found the question a body can ask that an arrow cannot; two of its rules are kept verbatim in panel 3 (see dna.dialects). ALSO READ: [[foresight_range]], the wave-1 series this one is built against, whose measured lesson about sub-pixel marks is applied here BEFORE the first capture rather than after it.

dna.default: law=dipole, coding=magnitude - a free design choice, because a synthesis has no shipped placements to preserve, and made for the strongest single reading rather than the source's. DIPOLE, NOT point_charge (which is [[force_field_visualizer]]'s shipped FieldType default), because dipole is the value where the four readings DISAGREE MOST and the disagreement is the exhibit: on the cancelling mid-line the glyphs shrink to almost nothing, the streamlines say the two sources are joined through exactly there, and the population says the region is a road rather than a place. It is also a SUM, so panel 4 prints an equation with two terms and the room's one function is visibly a superposition - and it is [[vector_fields]]' own shipped default pole census, so the room's default reading is a position the family already holds rather than a curator's invention. MAGNITUDE because it is the shipped default of both artifacts that carry `coding`, and because it is the reading where hue and length say the same thing, which is what the other three values are departures FROM.
dna.was: synthesized from force_field_visualizer, vector_field_grid, vector_fields, weather_vector_field, force_field_zone, particle_flow_swarm. Nothing was refactored and no source changed; this is a new object. The gap it fills: SIX artifacts drew a vector field, each with exactly ONE way of drawing it, and their registry notes argue at length about how the drawings relate - `poles is NOT law`, `field is NOT law`, `weather is deliberately not either` - while there has never been a place to LOOK at the relation. An axis shows one value per still, so a family whose members each own one rendering can only ever produce N separate pictures of N separate rooms. The question of whether four renderings of one field say the same thing needs at least two of them in one frame.
dna.axes_note: BOTH WORDS REUSED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, both value lists in the family's order, and NOT retyped: the room reads LAWS out of force_field_visualizer.gd and CODINGS out of vector_field_grid.gd at load (const LAW_SOURCE := preload(...)), the slot_machine pattern, so the vocabulary cannot drift from the family even if somebody edits the family. The literal @export_enum lines are written out as well, because the declaration gate reads the enum and GDScript cannot build one from a const; the two cannot disagree silently, since every word a map hands in is validated against the preloaded tables and anything unrecognised keeps the value already held. The two axes are ORTHOGONAL in the sense force_field_visualizer named for its own pair: `law` changes what is TRUE of the space, `coding` changes what the picture CLAIMS about it.
dna.coding_is_room_wide: This is the half of the second axis no source could have. Each of the six owns exactly one kind of picture, so each could only ever show the tint choice INSIDE that one kind. Held fixed across three different kinds at once - glyphs, ribbons, bodies - `coding` says that what the colour claims is separable from what kind of drawing you are looking at. It is applied to all three drawing panels and DELIBERATELY NOT to panel 4: a colour rule has no purchase on a symbol, and pretending otherwise would be decoration. It is also not applied to the source markers, which keep force_field_visualizer's own gold and blue at every value - a source is not a sample of the field, and tinting it by a rule about field values would be the one place in the room where the colour lied about what it encodes. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MEASUREMENT, stated before the sweep runs: one quarter of the wall is inert under `coding` by construction, which mechanically caps its frame-relative number at about three quarters of what an all-panel axis would score. Read it against that, not against `law`.
dna.one_arithmetic: The evidence_ladder rule, taken literally. `_field_at()` is the only place in the file a force is computed: the glyphs sample it, the streamline integrator marches it, the population marches the SAME integrator, and the plate prints it. The four panels cannot disagree about the physics by construction, which is a stronger guarantee than four functions that agree today. The arithmetic is force_field_visualizer's `_calculate_field` evaluated in ITS OWN unit frame - a 0.8 m square, its shipped field_size - with its own constants: the +0.01 softening in the inverse-square denominators, the 0.2 m dipole offset from a source_position that defaults to the origin, and the vortex profile d/(d^2 + 0.02). THE DIPOLE IS THEREFORE OFF-CENTRE, straddling 0 to +0.2 on a domain running -0.4 to +0.4. Centring it would be tidier and would not be its field. Only the drawing gauge is the room's: the unit square is mapped onto a 1.10 m panel.
dna.the_plane_is_stood_up: MEASURED DECISION, from a source's own still_note rather than from taste. Every one of the six draws its field on a HORIZONTAL plane. [[particle_flow_swarm]] measured what that costs on this bench - 'the rig's pitch is -0.26 rad, so the plane is seen at 15 degrees and foreshortened by 0.26' - and its whole subject peaked at 2.02% of frame, needing framing 0.6 before it could say anything. This room stands the field UP. At the sweep standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) four vertical panels project at cos(35.5) x cos(14.9) = 0.79 of their true area instead of 0.26, a factor of three before a single mark is drawn. Same law, same constants, x/z relabelled x/y. And under `gravity` it is not merely cheaper but necessary: a uniform downward field drawn flat on a table is 64 arrows seen end on, which is why force_field_visualizer's own streamlines at that value 'fall straight out of the plate'.
dna.dialects: A synthesis that flattens its members into examples has thrown away what they learned, so each panel renders in its source's own dialect with its source's own literals. GLYPHS: force_field_visualizer's grid_resolution of 8, its cell formula, its shaft-and-head MultiMesh pair, its 0.03 source-marker radius and its color_source / color_negative gold and blue, and no marker at all under gravity because there the source is a plane and not a point - its own reasoning for drawing parallel rules instead of rings at that value. STREAMLINES: its EV_STREAM_STEPS of 45 each way, its EV_STREAM_DT of 0.012, its normalised integrator ('so step length is uniform and a strong region does not eat the budget'), its stopping rule, and ribbons rather than line primitives for its stated reason - a line renders one pixel wide and would be measured as noise, a ribbon is geometry. POPULATION: [[particle_flow_swarm]]'s two rules verbatim - the wake is INTEGRATED BACKWARDS from the head rather than recorded, so it needs no history and is identical on frame one and frame one thousand; and a body reaching the domain edge is PARKED at the last point inside rather than wrapped, because the swarm's wrap-around is bookkeeping for keeping a plane populated and here it would claim a crossing the field never made. LAW: the equations and their glosses are force_field_visualizer's own _update_info strings, character for character, so the plate carries the source's words rather than a paraphrase.
dna.the_probe: The room's own device, and the thing that makes it more than four posters. One point, u* = (0.10, 0.16), marked by an identical ring in all three drawing panels and printed as two numbers on the fourth, so whatever else changes the four readings are demonstrably reading THE SAME POINT. It is not an arbitrary point: x = 0.10 is the perpendicular bisector of the dipole's two sources, where the vertical components cancel exactly and the sum comes out purely horizontal - F = (23.25, 0.00) at the default, a number that is neither of its two terms. That is what a superposition means, printed. The ring is white at every value of both axes; it is a fiducial, not a sample.
dna.gauge: THE LESSON [[foresight_range]] PAID A PASS FOR, APPLIED BEFORE THE FIRST CAPTURE INSTEAD OF AFTER IT. At this room's scale the frame carries roughly 200 px per metre, so a mark under about 0.022 m is under 5 px and an axis drawn in it is measuring a line width. The sources' own weights are bench weights: force_field_visualizer's 0.003 m ribbon half-width becomes 1.5 px here. So the marks are re-gauged to the ROOM - glyph shafts 0.011 m radius (4.5 px), heads 0.026 (10.5 px), ribbons 0.024 wide (4.9 px), particle heads 0.032 across (6.5 px), probe ring 0.088 across (18 px) - and the INTEGRATOR is untouched. THE ONE SOURCE LITERAL DELIBERATELY NOT KEPT is the streamline seed count: 5x5 at a resolvable ribbon width covers 90% of a 1.10 m plate, so the room seeds 4x4 and gets 16 curves at 4.9 px of ribbon with 14 px of gap. Holding the seed count would have forced a width the camera cannot resolve; holding the width would have flooded the panel. Recorded rather than buried, because it is the only number in this artifact that is not a source's. SEPARATELY: thickness is the room's pen and LENGTH is the field's magnitude - the arrow scale transform touches only the arrow's own axis, so a weak arrow is short and not thin, and the magnitude channel survives at every value of `coding`.
dna.declined: FIVE FAMILY WORDS REFUSED, each with a reason, and the refusals are as much of the design as the two words taken. `field` (vector_field_grid, particle_flow_swarm: cells|orbit|sink|saddle|shear) - PANEL 4 DECIDES IT. Four of those five values are the same linear rule x-dot = A*p with a different matrix, so the law plate would print one equation five times over; `law`'s four are four different equations with four different falloffs, which is what a room with a LAW PANEL in it needs. The corpus already holds these two words apart on this ground and the room simply lands on the side its fourth reading requires. `evidence` (force_field_visualizer, weather_vector_field) - the 2x2 layout ALREADY IS a disclosure ladder, samples then structure then effect then symbols, laid out in space rather than turned by a knob; declaring it as well would give the sweep two words for one drawing, which is the ground [[launch_arc]] refused `foresight` on. And an evidence axis on this host would have to hide whole panels, and a room that hides three quarters of itself is not four readings. `trace` (particle_flow_swarm: points|wake|streamline) - room-wide it DESTROYS the exhibit at one of its own values, because `streamline` drops head emphasis and turns each body into the field's integral curve, which is what panel 2 already is; one value of the axis would collapse two of the four readings into one. Panel 3 is pinned at `wake`, the rung where a body still has both a position and a history, and the pinning is the finding. `poles` (vector_fields: dipole|sink|source|binary) - it names what MAKES the field while `law` names which rule it obeys, a distinction vector_fields drew itself; here the two collide, since `dipole` is in both lists meaning the same picture and this room's `law` list already contains a superposition. `boundary` (force_field_zone: flow|cage|corners|open) - how a place declares its edge is mounting, not argument, and the plates and board must stand at every value because they are what pins the capture AABB. ALSO REFUSED: force_field_zone's OWN value list for the word `law` (gravity|lift|crossing|weightless). All four are UNIFORM vectors, one vector everywhere, and three of this room's four readings only say something when the field varies with position - under that list the streamlines would be parallel lines and the population a uniform drift at four headings. `gravity` appears in both lists meaning the same thing, which is the honesty test for a shared word and the one value the two lists agree on. FINALLY: panel_size, gutter and the lattice counts stay plain exports. Denser, bigger, more is a change of sampling, not of claim - both vector_field_grid and vector_fields declined exactly these and this room declines them for the same reason.
dna.no_emission: NOTHING IN THIS ROOM IS EMISSIVE, which is a departure from all six sources and is therefore recorded rather than left to be discovered. Under SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED the surface already renders at full albedo, ignoring the room's light, and emission is ADDED on top - so it costs twice here. On the INK it would whiten every mark equally, which would leave the geometry moving under `law` while `coding` measured nothing at all; the sources get away with emissive arrows because each sets its emission colour per material FROM the field value, whereas here one material serves hundreds of differently coloured MultiMesh instances and the colour has to arrive as albedo. On the MARKERS it clips: force_field_visualizer's gold (1.0, 0.8, 0.3) saturates its red and green at any emission above zero and lands on yellow, and the entire job of that marker under `dipole` is to be distinguishable from the blue one two panels over.
dna.determinism: The only randomness in the file is the population scatter, and it is SEEDED AT EVERY VALUE INCLUDING THE DEFAULT - population_seed = 3, with no 0-means-unseeded path of the kind both particle_flow_swarm and vector_fields had to keep for their existing placements. This artifact has no placements to keep faith with, so it simply has no unseeded branch. There is no _process, no timer, no physics body, no Area3D, no player and no shader clock, so nothing is time-domain and nothing is frame-rate dependent: one still is a complete account at any value. That is why dna.fixture is empty rather than absent.
dna.fixture_why: Empty, and deliberately. The two things a fixture normally supplies here do not exist: there is no gate on a player, a controller, an XR rig or a map, so _ready builds the whole room unconditionally; and there is no unseeded draw to pin, because the one RNG is seeded by default. population_seed is left in apply_grid_config so a room can RE-DEAL the cloud, never so it can un-seed it. No typed bool is exposed to a token either - both axes are String enums and the two dimensions are floats - which is the trap that cost the prompter's box a pass.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED, NOT MEASURED - captures are serialised centrally and none was run for this artifact, so treat this as a starting point with an arithmetic behind it rather than a result. The union box is 2.42 x 2.55 x 0.34 m and is IDENTICAL at every value of both axes, because every mark either axis controls lies inside the panel plates: radius 1.766, and dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with PAD = 1.9, so the visible half-extent is 1.9 * 1.766 * framing. At 0.55 that is a visible extent of 3.69 m against a subject projecting 2.18 m wide (2.42*cos(35.5) + 0.34*sin(35.5)) by 2.55 m tall - 59% of the frame width and 69% of its height. 0.50 was computed and rejected: it gives 65% x 76%, which fits a square frame and CLIPS the top and bottom of a 4:3 one, and the aspect ratio was not verified. THE TYPOGRAPHIC FLOOR THAT STOPPED [[foresight_range]] AT 0.48 DOES NOT EXIST HERE, and that is a design decision rather than luck: every Label3D is UNBILLBOARDED and lies in the wall plane inside the panel it captions, so the text is inside the box the rig fits to instead of hanging outside it unmeasured. Widest string is force_field_visualizer's own 'F = tangent(r) x profile(|r|)' at 29 characters, which at font 18 and pixel_size 0.0034 is about 0.89 m against a 1.10 m panel.
dna.budget: About 29 nodes at the default: 1 backing board, 2 feet, 4 panel plates, 4 panel roots, 3 MultiMeshInstance3D (glyph shafts, glyph heads, population), 1 MeshInstance3D of ImmediateMesh ribbons, up to 6 source markers (2 under dipole x 3 panels; none at all under gravity), 3 probe rings and 5 Label3D. MultiMesh instances total 968 - 64 shafts, 64 heads, and 120 bodies at 7 instances each. No collision shapes, no static bodies, nothing to grab. Two orders of magnitude under the ~3200 element budget, and the MultiMesh carries only marks that sit inside plates the AABB already covers, so no layers=0 anchor is needed and none would be honest: a wall's footprint IS its extent.
dna.still_note: Everything this artifact argues is standing geometry - nothing moves, nothing fires, nothing is timed - so the difference between two values of either axis is the presence, position and colour of marks in fixed places, which is exactly what survives a shutter. EXPECT `law` TO BE THE STRONG AXIS: it redraws all 64 arrows, all 16 streamlines and all 120 bodies at once, moves or removes the source markers, and swaps the equation AND the two probe numbers on the fourth panel. `coding` is the thinner one by construction - it changes no geometry at all, only the colour of the ink in three of the four panels - and both artifacts that carry the word warned about exactly this dilution on hosts with far less ink than this one. THE PREDICTIONS, so they can be wrong on the record: law well above 5%, coding between 1.5% and 3%, with magnitude-against-direction the widest coding pair (a two-colour ramp replaced by the whole hue circle, which is the value vector_field_grid also expected to bite hardest) and magnitude-against-banded the narrowest. IF `coding` COMES BACK NEAR ZERO, check in this order: (1) that the ink materials are still unshaded WITHOUT emission - an emissive white added on top of a vertex colour whitens every mark equally and would leave `law` moving while `coding` measured nothing, which is the failure this file's _ink() comment exists to prevent; (2) crop to one panel before concluding anything, per vector_field_grid's own instruction; (3) remember that panel 4 is inert under `coding` by design and caps the frame-relative number at about three quarters. IF `law` comes back near zero the fault is upstream of the design, because the four fields share no geometry whatever. THE PAIR TO WATCH on `law` is point_charge against vortex: same single source, same falloff family, same marker - only the rotation differs, and in the glyph panel a rotated arrow of the same length at the same place is the thinnest difference this axis can produce.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: COMPUTED BEFORE THE SWEEP by re-implementing _field_at and the log tone in Python, so it is not discovered later and mistaken for a fault. AT law=gravity, (coding=magnitude) AND (coding=banded) ARE THE SAME PICTURE TO THE BYTE. Every sample of a uniform field has |F| = 1.00 exactly, so the peak is 1.00, every tone is 1.00, and both a continuous ramp and a four-band quantisation of it return the same hot end. A ramp and a legend cannot disagree about a field with one value in it. That is the axis telling the truth about what `gravity` IS - the value force_field_visualizer itself describes as the only one where position carries no information - and it is the same shape as [[particle_flow_swarm]]'s (sink, points) against (sink, wake) measuring 0.02% apart at a stagnation point. The other two coding values still separate there: `uniform` goes pale and `direction` paints one flat hue. AT law=vortex the same pair is NARROW but not zero: the vortex profile is bounded, so the measured tone spans only 0.70 to 1.00 across the lattice and the top two bands cover almost all of it. Measured tone ranges, for whoever reads the sweep: gravity 1.00-1.00, vortex 0.70-1.00, point_charge 0.38-1.00, dipole 0.23-1.00. `coding` has the most to say under dipole, which is a second reason the default sits there.
dna.known_gap: No map places this yet, and the corpus's standing warning applies with full force: exactly one map anywhere places any artifact at a non-default axis value. A room whose whole point is holding four renderings at ONE law is worth nothing until somebody writes field_room#law:vortex in a map and stands in front of it. The second half of the gap is specific to this synthesis: its six sources are spread across four registry files and three sequences (change, vectors, physicssimulation, forces), and none of those rooms currently has any reason to know the others exist.
